chunks: Abu Saʿid al-Mukārī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has exempted women from four things: raising the voice in the talbiyah, the saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah—meaning brisk walking—entering the Kaʿbah, and touching the Black Stone.

key_terms.السَّعْيَ: the ritual movement between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah
key_terms.الْإِجْهَارَ: raising the voice openly or audibly
key_terms.الْحَجَرِ الْأَسْوَدِ: the Black Stone set in the Kaʿbah
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: the Kaʿbah, the sacred House in Makkah
key_terms.بِالتَّلْبِيَةِ: with the talbiyah, the pilgrim’s devotional proclamation during hajj

ai.seo_question: Which hajj practices are women exempted from in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning certain rites of hajj for women. It explains that women are exempted from four specific practices, including raising the voice in the talbiyah and brisk running during saʿy, indicating distinctions in ritual performance.
